plan.topic: First weeks on tirzepatide: when stomach side effects usually show up and when they tend to ease (label timing wording)
plan.angle: Spin-off of L1, 20:00 funnel, standard arm. It asks one fresh question rather than re-cutting the L1 script. Sentence 1: 'Starting tirzepatide and wondering when the queasy part hits?' By 6 s: in the trials, nausea, diarrhoea and vomiting happened mostly while the dose was being increased and decreased over time. Use label wording, framed as a trial pattern, not a prediction, with numbers matching L1's verified script exactly. Untagged tips: smaller meals, eat slowly, stop at comfortably full, sip fluids unless you've been told to limit them. Emergency card: severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting → stop and call your healthcare provider right away. Then the scoped don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and the closing line. No Exp F line, no dose numbers. Post note: related-video target is L1 once it's verified live, otherwise Side Effects.

package.title: Tirzepatide Nausea: Does It Ease Over Time? #shorts
package.description:
Tirzepatide nausea came mostly during dose increases and decreased over time in the pooled weight trials (1 in 4+ on tirzepatide vs about 1 in 12 on placebo). A pattern, not a promise.

Severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting, can signal pancreatitis. Stop and call your healthcare provider right away. For anything else, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.

Source: Zepbound (tirzepatide) Prescribing Information, section 6.1, revised 08/2026: https://uspl.lilly.com/zepbound/zepbound.html?s=pi

#Tirzepatide #GLP1

Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

If you've started tirzepatide and you've felt a little queasy early on, you're far from alone. In the pooled weight trials, nausea hit about one in four or more people on tirzepatide (vs roughly one in twelve on placebo), and in those trials it showed up mostly around dose increases and decreased over time. script.cta: Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description. [Post note, not spoken: 20:00 funnel slot, no Exp F line. factcheck.summary: I checked every number and claim against the live Zepbound label (revised 8/2026). Table 1, pooled Study 1 and Study 2 (the weight-reduction trials), shows nausea at 25%, 29% and 28% on 5, 10 and 15 mg versus 8% on placebo. So "one in four or more" and "about one in twelve" on placebo are both accurate. The label's own sentence, "The majority of nausea, vomiting, and/or diarrhea events occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time", supports s2 word for word. The pancreatitis warning is accurate, keeps "right away" and has the emergency scoping. The fluids tip has a caveat for people told to limit fluids, and there is no dosing or switching advice. The spoken word count is 119, which I counted myself and which fits the tight arm (90–120). Sentence 1 names tirzepatide in 12 words. All the issues are minor packaging and sourcing polish. Because the script is at 119 of 120 words, every fix below either adds no spoken words or swaps words one for one.
